Santa María Tulpetlac is located in Ecatepec, in the State of Mexico. The site's pilgrimage history is connected with Juan Bernardino, Juan Diego's uncle: according to the Guadalupe tradition, Our Lady appeared to him and healed him of an illness.

The Sanctuary of the Fifth Apparition of Our Lady of Guadalupe commemorates this event. Inside, visitors can see an image of the apparition and an altar area dedicated to Our Lady as "Health of the Sick". A visit to Tulpetlac extends the Guadalupe pilgrimage route beyond the basilica in Mexico City and offers an introduction to local religious life.

## Tulum — Yucatán's Premier Tourist Destination!

Tulum is a remarkable place on the eastern coast of the Yucatán Peninsula. It has three distinct areas: the ruins of the old Maya city, the area's main attraction; the Indigenous town of Tulum Pueblo; and a tourism and leisure zone with some of the best hotels and beaches along the road and the Caribbean Sea.

## Tulum — The Perfect Mix of Experiences!

Tulum is considered the Maya's only seaport and is one of the region's best-known archaeological sites. The city, perched on the edge of a sheer cliff, offers magnificent views of the sea. Stone walls surround it on three sides, while the seaward side is protected by steep cliffs rising fifteen metres above the shore. Tulum's beaches are excellent, and travellers come to enjoy everything the destination has to offer: tropical scenery, dramatic cliffs, fine white sand, exceptionally clear turquoise water and a beautiful underwater world. Romance, exotic surroundings, archaeology and village life come together here in an appealing blend.

## White Beaches and Jungle: What to See in Tumbes, Peru

### Tumbes — A Seaside Resort in Peru!

Tumbes is located on Peru's northern coast, only 30 km from the border with Ecuador.

## Relaxing in Tumbes

### Tumbes — Beautiful White-Sand Beaches!

The city's entire coastline is lined with white-sand beaches. The surrounding area has mangroves, dry equatorial forest in Cerros de Amotape National Park and humid tropical forest in the city's protected area. Around 30% of Tumbes is designated as a protected natural area, so a beach holiday here comes with fresh air and lush vegetation. Puerto Pizarro Beach, 13 km from the city, is the most popular with visitors.

The Tumbira community is visited with a guide during journeys along the Rio Negro. This stop offers a glimpse of inhabited riverbanks and an opportunity to learn about the lives of local people.

On river-cruise itineraries, a visit to Tumbira is combined with the Seringal Rubber Plantation Museum and time relaxing on a river beach. For the community itself, the main focus of the visit is meeting residents and discovering their riverside settlement.
